# Proposed P-Theorem-C source/import inventory

This is a descriptive proposal for a separate omission/applicability reader, not a graph, theorem-status table, proof derivation or completeness certificate.

## Frozen source and extraction convention

Math- commit 9fd261135b41daf1e377f9ef2db193fee6ec36be. P blob dfed3b8d318a3ab1950957f393307733a4bef3f2 (40261B), §§10–15: section-heading boundary lines310–481, payload lines312–480. Each maximal contiguous nonempty nonheading block is one source unit; displayed multi-line equations remain one block. Blocks B01–B66 are exhaustive for that declared syntactic boundary. Narrative, displays and lead-ins all remain represented; zero-use lead-ins/results are not silently dropped. This denominator measures extraction coverage only.

A claimed input-use occurrence is one explicitly listed input/application within a row. Repeat use of the same interface in another actual consuming location is counted again. A display paired with its lead-in is not counted as an additional input solely because it repeats the conclusion. Context citations, definitions, reading corrections and scope guards are recorded but do not become new inferential premises. These choices are proposed and may be amended by an omission reader; neither the count nor a citation validates applicability.

The proposed syntactic denominator is66 blocks: §10=11, §11=10, §12=8, §13=19, §14=5, §15=13. The input-use list below contains 109 occurrences. It is not a claim that the proof has exactly 109 atomic logical premises; proof granularity and every unnamed mechanism remain subject to separate source-owner/omission review.

## Explicit unknowns and omission/applicability exit

This is not full proof completeness. Earlier P proofs, CAP's derivation, E2's external KR base, ordinary Morse/H0 once-counting bookkeeping and genericity arguments are imported or asserted at the listed locations and remain unexpanded here. The supplied interface at P14/l445 identifies finite ordinary bars; it is not a Lean persistence-module alignment theorem. Every ordinary/global-elder interface must retain its actual hypotheses and reading set. The mathematical validity of each edge is not assessed by this inventory.

R is a SEPARATE quantitative remainder consumer (REC §7/l211); its all-mark O(1) result and the separately frozen CUB physical-axial derivation are not premises of P-C. C52 is a separate whole-torus occurrence/field-first consumer. Neither expected count per volume nor its coefficient is silently changed into an occurrence probability. C50/C51 auxiliary witness/reciprocal statements are not inserted. No CJ certified-J outcome or numeric certificate is inferred.

Separate reader instructions:
1. Reproduce the declared66-block syntax against exact P bytes, checking each block's line locator. A source-boundary omission is an extraction finding; a zero-use block is still in the denominator.
2. Challenge each listed input-use and split or merge proposed occurrences with a precise consuming sentence/equation. Search each narrative block for unnamed implications omitted from the list; do not treat a unique-lemma list as an occurrence inventory.
3. Validate applicability separately: original b,k,r,d,L/frame quantifiers, typed/full normalizer, ordinary sphere, ordered roles, per-volume convention, limit order, exact shrinking-k cutoff, unconditional far bound, finite ordinary-bar once-counting and parity rather than isotropy. Context and corrections cannot masquerade as proof premises.
4. Independently inspect mandatory CAP/E1/E2/REC consumption boundaries. Do not expand to CAP numerical §§6+ or silently add R, C52, C50/C51. Mark missing external/conventional derivations UNKNOWN rather than inventing supplied lemmas.
5. Return scoped omissions/amendments and a proposed denominator disposition to the existing281 discussion. Source custodians and later independent readers decide applicability/accepted edges. No automatic graph/status/schema mutation or theorem verdict follows.

Own completion will be only delivery/release of this proposed inventory. The full leading-order goal retains its separate CUB convention, blind reconstruction, Lean semantics, finite-L scope and numerical obligations.
